newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's miners survive gold fall - analyst.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's miners survive gold fall - analyst.

text.p: Austraia's gold mining industry remains fundamentally sound despite the recent dive in the gold price, industry analyst group Surbiton Associates Pty Ltd said on Thursday.
The average weighted cash cost of production among three quarters of Australia's gold miners surveyed by the group was A$369 an ounce for the September quarter versus A$372 in the previous quarter.
"Even using this simplistic measure, there is still a considerable cash margin for most producers at current prices," the group said.
Gold prices are hovering at US$358 an ounce on world bullion markets, the lowest price in over three years.
About 80 percent of the gold produced in Australia in the September quarter was at a cash cost below A$450 an ounce, Surbiton said.
This compares with a current spot price of around A$455 an ounce.
Between 34 percent and 50 percent of gold production was at a cash cost below A$350 an ounce, figures from the survey show.
Between 24 and 35 percent of production was at a cost under A$300 an ounce, while between eight and 11 percent had cash costs below A$250 an ounce.
Eagle Mining Corp NL's Nimary gold mine in Western Australia recorded the lowest cash cost at an average of A$203 an ounce, Surbiton said.
Eagle mines ore from Nimary grading 5.5 grammes of gold per tonne, making it one of Australia's richest lodes.
The Australian index of leading gold mining companies has fallen 6.6 percent so far this year, and at one stage on Thursday fell to its lowest since November 1995.
